This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking enhancement of compensation in MVC No.1071/2015 dated 26.10.2016 passed on the file of the V Additional District & Sessions Judge, Additional MACT, Shivamogga, Sitting At Sagar.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Judge, Additional MACT, Shivamogga, Sitting At Sagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.3.
Notice to respondent Nos.1 and 2 are dispensed with.
NC: 2025:KHC:30706 HC-KAR 3.
Injured/claimant filed claim application claiming compensation of Rs.17,45,000.
However, the tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, granted an amount of Rs.1,38,687/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant suffered multiple fractures, but the amount granted was meager.
Further contended that the appellant was aged 28 years, working as a plumber cum electrician and he sustained total functional disability.
He could not handle a hammer and heavy equipment.
However, the said fact was not considered by the tribunal.
A meager amounts were granted for pain and suffering.
Also, the appellant sustained another 100% functional disability.
Therefore, requested for NC: 2025:KHC:30706 HC-KAR enhancement of compensation.

As per Ex.P5/wound certificate, appellant sustained the following injuries;
1) Fracture of left clavicle.

sentences.text: Further, they produced X-rays under Ex.P7.

PW2 stated that he was admitted as inpatient and undergone surgery on 20.10.2014 and locking plate was inserted to the shoulder and many fragments were inserted to the right hand and discharged on 23.10.2014
Thereafter, he attended follow-up treatment subsequently fractures were united.
PW2 further stated that though he treated the appellant for 9 days, appellant took follow up treatment till 15.06.2016.
Accident occurred on 16.10.2014 and thus he took treatment for 12 months.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant mainly contended that there was 100% disability, but it was not considered by the tribunal.

It is also stated that as per NC: 2025:KHC:30706 HC-KAR the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, if a person sustains accident in the year 2014,
notional income of Rs.8,500/- per month is to be taken, but the tribunal erred in taking Rs.6,000/-
only.
6. Learned counsel for the appellate further stated that doctor specifically stated that he could not handle the hammer and heavy equipment in view of injury sustained by the petitioner.

Admittedly,
petitioner was a plumber cum electrician aged 29 years.
Considering the nature of injuries and his occupation, this court finds that it is just and reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards the injuries.
Also, as he could not do any work, considering the nature of injuries, this court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of loss of earnings for 6 months, Rs.8,500/- X 6 = Rs.51,000/-.
Loss of amenities of Rs.15000/- holds good and attendant charges will be enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
Nourishment and conveyance granted to Rs.20,000/-.
NC: 2025:KHC:30706 HC-KAR 7.
Thus in all, this Court has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:
